historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes reboot risk but assumes setup token equivalence and cannot prove graphical firmware entry, no-setting-change behavior or safe exit; it also exposes credentials.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly retains automatable boot control while requiring a human visual oracle and an explicit no-save boundary inside firmware setup.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The acceptance point is a recognizable firmware setup page, not merely POST pause or a command return. Because setup UI itself enables persistent configuration, entry evidence and exit-without-save evidence must bracket a no-mutation interval.

original_test_intent: Validate that the BMC's enabled one-time BiosSetup setting enters the intended firmware setup interface on the approved SUT, without changing or saving BIOS configuration, and then restores normal boot.
original_method: Record BIOS identity, configuration digest or approved comparison and normal boot state; validate the vendor BiosSetup/setup mapping and expected visual marker; obtain approval, apply/read back the protected one-time override, reboot once, have an operator confirm the correct setup page, capture evidence without navigating mutable controls, exit explicitly without saving, then prove the override is consumed, BIOS settings unchanged and the OS path restored.
manual_activity: An authorized operator visually confirms the exact firmware setup page, avoids mutable controls and exits without saving; the owner approves the reboot and controls recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: BIOS access credential handling if required
Baseline BIOS setting evidence or digest
safety_requirements: Do not infer setup entry from bootdev success
Use protected credentials and one-time scope
Human must verify the exact setup screen
Do not edit, reset defaults, update firmware or save configuration
Stop on password lockout, wrong screen, change prompt, update prompt or timeout
Exit without saving and compare BIOS state
Clear override, restore OS boot and preserve logs
agent_execution_scope: Collect boot and BIOS identity/configuration baseline
Apply/read back one approved setting after confirmation
Request and perform one approved reboot
Collect timing and screenshots supplied by the operator
Verify no configuration delta, override consumption and OS recovery
Report evidence without visual substitution or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target, mapping and reboot window
Provide authorized visual operator and recovery
Recover any lockout or unexpected change

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: bootdev setup is potentially applicable only after vendor mapping; the literal command exposes credentials, resets immediately and cannot prove a visual setup page, no mutation, exit behavior or cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the protected vendor-mapped one-time setup control and structured readback; rely on an authorized operator for the setup-screen and exit-without-save oracle, then compare BIOS state and restore boot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BiosSetup, Enabled/Save, reboot and 10/20-minute estimates remain; specific path is the documented setup screen.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bracket the visual setup session with boot-control readback and BIOS configuration evidence, recording entry marker, time in UI, keys/actions used, explicit discard/exit choice and post-boot configuration comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines setup acceptance and proves the UI visit did not become a configuration test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A setup boot flag does not show that firmware entered the intended UI, while a screenshot alone does not show that settings were left unchanged or the override was consumed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A stray key, timeout default or privileged prompt can persist settings or lock access; visual evidence must omit secrets and recovery must not blindly reset CMOS/defaults.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define the recognizable setup page and safe exit sequence. Any BIOS setting modification belongs to a separate governed testcase; the copied PXE note is not BiosSetup acceptance.
expected_evidence: Approved target/window, BIOS identity/version, setup mapping/marker and baseline configuration evidence
Protected one-time BiosSetup write/readback and reboot request
POST/console timeline and redacted visual confirmation of the exact setup page
Operator action log and explicit exit-without-save/no-change proof
Consumed override, unchanged BIOS comparison and normal OS restoration
Health, audit/SEL/OS logs, recovery actions and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and procedure consistently request BiosSetup entry. The specific path is the firmware setup screen; the copied PXE note is unrelated context rather than a competing target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The mapping, visual marker, console and exit procedure are normal owner/vendor prerequisites; execution is gated until provided but the test remains understandable.

review_improvement: Defines a visually verifiable setup-entry checkpoint and proves no firmware configuration was changed before returning to normal boot.
independent_technical_reasoning: BIOS Setup is both a destination and a mutation surface. Merely reaching it satisfies the boot-path objective, whereas saving any value expands the test and changes recovery risk. A pre/post configuration comparison plus a recorded discard exit separates successful navigation from unintended persistent configuration.
